why: A (universes at 0) has exists_isomorphic_of_isomorphic (every y ∈ F⁻¹(x) has an isomorphic y' ∈ F⁻¹(x')), fiberIndex_eq (π(F⁻¹(x)) = π(F⁻¹(x'))), lemma_8_6_2 and lemma_8_6_2_equiv. A_to_B: B's 'before the lemma' claim is transitivity of ≅. For an arbitrary enumeration Θ of the classes of F⁻¹(x), it sets Θ'_j = {y' ∈ F⁻¹(x') | ∃ y ∈ Θ_j, y ≅ y'}. A's exists_isomorphic_of_isomorphic (for x ≅ x' and x' ≅ x) makes these nonempty and covering; the rest is class bookkeeping. B_to_A is proved only by re-proving A outright from the non-item existsUnique_lift; B is not used. That is forced. B's matching condition only constrains isomorphic pairs y ∈ F⁻¹(x), y' ∈ F⁻¹(x'), plus equally many (q) classes. It never says that a point of F⁻¹(x) has an isomorphic partner in F⁻¹(x'). If there were no such pairs, every enumeration of the q classes of F⁻¹(x') would satisfy B's conclusion. So the totality of the correspondence, which is A's exists_isomorphic_of_isomorphic, fiberIndex_eq and lemma_8_6_2_equiv, is content of A that B lacks. B transcribes the lemma's sentence literally; the totality is in the text's proof (lifting x → x' through Definition 8.5.1 (3)).
